item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00393","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C03","C21"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both are congressional advocacy letters about Point IV or closely integrated foreign-assistance funding, and both use the same distinctive argumentative sequence: assistance gives hope and protects freedom against communism; the program supplies practical help to underdeveloped peoples; reducing or failing to enact the full funding would cause grave harm; and American action serves as visible evidence of national resolve. C03 is closely related in subject matter and explicitly connects aid, practical development, underdeveloped areas, and political stability, but its detailed Palestine-refugee machinery is less directly reflected in the child. C21 shares the urgent foreign-aid appropriation appeal and free-world security framing, but concerns military rather than Point IV assistance.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Point IV program has come to be a symbol of hope for millions of people all over the world","parent_excerpt":"Approval of this measure will give renewed hope and vigor to people everywhere who are working to achieve their economic independence and maintain their political freedom.","explanation":"Both frame foreign assistance as a source of hope that sustains political freedom."},{"child_excerpt":"only through such action as the Point IV program can we demonstrate that fact in concrete and practical terms","parent_excerpt":"The Act will authorize the carrying forward of the vital program of technical and other assistance to under-developed countries...
